title: SLO Lite: FastPath for Small Services — Cross-Functional Rollout Plan
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a lightweight, repeatable path ("SLO Lite / FastPath") to apply SLO guardrails to small services with minimal friction. Goal: get >60% of small, low-risk services covered by meaningful SLOs in 90 days without heavy engineering lift.

Context and motivation
- We have a backlog of small services (cron jobs, aux APIs, internal tooling endpoints) that are uninstrumented or have no measurable SLOs.
- Full SLO onboarding is valuable but often blocked by instrumentation work, dashboarding, and lengthy product reviews.
- Small services still cause outages and carry operational debt. A pragmatic, lower-effort approach will increase reliability coverage and reduce incident blast radius.

Goals (90-day target)
- 60% of identified small services have a working SLO and alerting (SLO Lite)
- Mean time to onboard per service <= 3 business days for services in FastPath cohort
- Automated dashboarding template available and used by 75% of FastPath onboardings

Principles for SLO Lite
- Keep it practical: measurable, achievable, and reviewable within a week.
- Minimal instrumentation: prefer existing telemetry (edge/load-balancer, gateway, or app-level counters) over large refactors.
- Standardized template: a single, opinionated SLO template to avoid long debates.
- Incremental rigor: services can graduate to full SLOs later.

SLO Lite Template (opinionated)
- Objective: Availability SLO + one latency SLI (optional)
- Availability SLO: "successful responses / total requests" measured over a 14-day rolling window, target 99% (or team-defined higher bar for customer-facing flows)
- Latency SLI (optional): P95 request latency under X ms (choose X based on service category: internal tooling 500ms, user-facing 200ms) over 7-day window
- Alerting: burn-rate style alert when 14-day error budget burn-rate > 2x for more than 30 minutes OR a single-day drop below 95% availability

Selection criteria for FastPath cohort
- Surface area: service serves internal users or small set of downstream consumers (<= 5 teams)
- Risk: no direct external customer billing impact, non-critical to core latency SLOs
- Observability: at least one pre-existing metric or log-based proxy metric available (e.g., nginx 5xx, gateway latency)
- Team capacity: owner identifies an engineer to run the 1–3 day onboarding steps

Instrumentation checklist (minimal)
- Identify a source SLI (choose one): LB/gateway success rate, app-level 2xx counter, or operation-specific event counter
- Verify tag keys: service, environment (prod/stage), endpoint path or route
- Create a metric rollup or log-based metric if needed (example queries included in the onboarding template)
- Hook metric into standard alerting policy (SLO Lite policy)

FastPath onboarding steps (2–3 business days, template)
Day 0: Kickoff (30–60m)
- Owner: service lead + oncall SRE liaison
- Outcome: pick SLI source, agree on target (default 99%), create jira ticket SRE-1120-<service>
Day 1: Metric creation & dashboard (2–4h)
- SRE runs helper script or Terraform module to create metric & dashboard from template
- Owner verifies numbers for 1 day of history
Day 2: Alerting + review (1–3h)
- Attach SLO to existing alerting channels, set burn-rate thresholds, sanity-check with oncall rota
- Quick review: product/owner signoff in Slack thread or PR comment
Optional Day 3: Improve tags or add latency SLI (if team opts in)

Automation and tooling to accelerate FastPath
- CLI tooling: 'slo-lite init <service>' will scaffold dashboard + metric queries + SLO object (see github/infra/telemetry#342)
- Terraform module: reusable metric creation + alert policy resource for standard buckets
- One-click dashboard template in Console: a FastPath view with SLI, SLO, burn-rate and incident links

RACI (cross-functional)
- SRE (liaison): facilitator, owns template and automation, runs initial onboarding for first 10 services
- Service owner: provides access to logs/metrics, validates targets, owns long-term maintenance
- Observability (telemetry infra): helps add log-based metrics, verifies scrape configs
- Product/Manager: optional signoff for public services

Cohort plan and cadence (first 90 days)
- Week 0: Pilot (5 services) — identify 2 pilot SRE liaisons and automation smoke test
- Weeks 1–4: Fast ramp (25 services) — run batch onboards, tune templates, collect feedback
- Weeks 5–12: Broad rollout (up to 100 services) — handoff to service owners, SRE moves to a support/advisory role

Success metrics and signals
- Coverage: % of targeted small services with SLO object created
- Onboarding time: median time from kickoff → working SLO
- Incident impact: number of incidents mitigated early due to SLO alerts (post-hoc review)
- Template reuse: number of times CLI/TF module used

Communication plan
- Weekly sync (30m) during ramp: SRE liaison + product + observable infra reps; capture notes in Confluence page (linked)
- Slack channel: #sre-slo-lite for quick questions and signals
- Monthly stakeholder note: short metric snapshot and top 3 blockers sent to platform leadership

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: teams adopt SLO Lite but don’t maintain; Mitigation: automated monthly heartbeat check and SRE nudges; escalate to manager if no maintenance in 60 days
- Risk: metric semantics drift (false positives/negatives); Mitigation: require owner signoff and store SLI query in repo/PR history
- Risk: too many low-quality SLOs; Mitigation: SRE-run quality-spot audits for first 30 onboardings, apply checklist scoring

Gating and graduation
- Graduation criteria to full SLO program: evidence of owner maintenance, instrumentation robustness (per checklist), and business impact > threshold for full SLO investment
- Services that fail to maintain after 90 days default to quarterly check-ins and potential decommission review

Operational play: incident surface flow
- When SLO Lite alert fires: oncall uses SLO dashboard quick-links to jump to traces/logs; if incident requires cross-team escalation, SRE liaison opens a postmortem template and tags the service as candidate for improved SLI coverage

Open questions / decisions needed
- Default availability target: should we use 99.5% for internal user-facing vs 99% for low-risk? (decision table proposed)
- Approval flow: is Slack signoff sufficient or do we require a ticketed product approval for public services?
- Resource allocation: can SRE allocate 1 FTE equivalent for 6 weeks to run ramp?

Next steps (immediate)
- Approve SLO Lite template and CLI module into main repo (owners: Marco Liu & Sofia Chen) — target 2026-06-22
- Identify pilot services (owner: product & platform leads) — target 2026-06-19
- Schedule pilot kickoff and weekly ramp syncs (owner: Aisha Patel) — target 2026-06-18

Appendix: Quick checklist for service owner (copyable)
- Have a metric source (LB, gateway, or app counter)
- Run `slo-lite init` or request SRE to scaffold
- Validate SLO numbers for at least 24h
- Join review in Slack and approve alerting rule
- Commit SLI query to repo and link in SLO object
